result.sentence: Moving 200 kWh a day cuts about 9.9 metric tons of CO₂ a year.

work.method: CO₂ avoided = kWh a day × (current − proposed typical intensity) ÷ 1,000 × days. Typical intensities are EIA-930 consumption-based CO₂ intensity, the median for each local clock hour of each month over the latest three complete years, averaged over the hours of each window and weighted by days in each month.
steps: Intensity difference: 1,000 − 700 lb/MWh = 300 lb/MWh, or 0.3 lb/kWh.
200 kWh a day × 0.3 lb/kWh × 365 days = 21,900 lb a year less.
21,900 lb ÷ 2204.62 lb per metric ton = 9.93 metric tons.
An estimate from history using average-intensity (attributional) accounting: not a forecast, and not the actual change in grid emissions, which depends on the marginal generators.
assumptions: The load is spread evenly over the hours of each window.
The same daily energy moves on every day of the year.

citations.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Hourly Electric Grid Monitor (Form EIA-930)
citations.locator: CO2 Emissions Intensity for Consumed Electricity (lb/kWh)
